x-e-e5-01.title: 'Most popular' - does the text back it up?
x-e-e5-01.goal: Think about whether the number information in the text supports a claim (popular), and make an English question that could check the claim.
x-e-e5-01.material:
Mina's class has a reading corner with a bookshelf.

Our class has a reading corner. There are 20 books on the shelf. Twelve of them are about animals. Four are about space, and four are story books. The teacher did not buy any new books this year.

Mina says, "Animal books are the most popular in our class."
x-e-e5-01.thinking.0: Compare the claim with the details of the text
x-e-e5-01.thinking.1: Tell what 'is there' from what 'gets read'
x-e-e5-01.thinking.2: Make a question that fills the missing evidence
x-e-e5-01.prereq.0: Easy words such as most, popular, and about
x-e-e5-01.prereq.1: Number words such as Twelve and four
x-e-e5-01.s.s1.prompt: Judge whether the text supports Mina's words (animal books are the most popular).
x-e-e5-01.s.s1.hint.0: Think about what 'popular' means in Mina's words, and look for a sentence in the text that tells you that.
x-e-e5-01.s.s1.hint.1: Think about whether 'how many are on the shelf' and 'how many times students read them' are the same information.
x-e-e5-01.s.s1.o.a: The evidence is enough. 12 of the 20 books are animal books, so students will probably read them the most.
x-e-e5-01.s.s1.r.a: Look back at whether you treated the number of books and the number of times they were read as the same thing.
x-e-e5-01.s.s1.o.b: The evidence is not enough. It has only the number of books, and it does not say which books students read.
x-e-e5-01.s.s1.r.b: I compared whether the information the claim needs and the information the text gives are the same.
x-e-e5-01.s.s1.o.c: The evidence is enough. The teacher did not buy new books, so students will read only old books.
x-e-e5-01.s.s1.r.c: Check whether 'did not buy new books' connects to which books are popular.
x-e-e5-01.s.s1.explain: The text only tells the number of books on the shelf (12 animal books, etc.). It does not say which books students read or borrow a lot, so we cannot check the claim 'most popular'.
x-e-e5-01.s.s2.prompt: To check whether Mina's words are right, what question should you ask the students? Write one English question sentence.
x-e-e5-01.s.s2.hint.0: Pick one action that shows 'popular' (reading, borrowing, choosing).
x-e-e5-01.s.s2.hint.1: Write a question that asks about that action, and put a question mark at the end.
x-e-e5-01.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Does the answer to my question tell 'which books they read a lot'?
x-e-e5-01.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Does it ask about what students do, rather than asking for the number of books?
x-e-e5-01.s.s2.modelNote.1: Another good question that checks with the number of times borrowed.

x-e-e5-02.title: Find and fix the wrong line in Jin's summary
x-e-e5-02.topic: Reading short texts, ads, and messages
x-e-e5-02.goal: Compare a short text and a summary line by line, find the line that goes against the text, and rewrite it in English.
x-e-e5-02.material:
A short text about Ben.

Ben went to the lake on Saturday. He wanted to fish, but it rained in the morning, so he stayed at his uncle's house and played cards. In the afternoon the rain stopped. Ben and his uncle walked to the lake and caught two fish. They cooked the fish for dinner.
x-e-e5-02.thinking.0: Check each line of the summary against the sentences of the text
x-e-e5-02.thinking.1: Check the order of events and the time (morning/afternoon)
x-e-e5-02.thinking.2: Rewrite a sentence to fit the text
x-e-e5-02.prereq.0: Easy words such as rain, lake, fish, and cook
x-e-e5-02.prereq.1: The meanings of morning and afternoon
x-e-e5-02.s.s1.prompt: Jin summarized this text in four lines. Choose the line that does not match the text.
x-e-e5-02.s.s1.hint.0: Read the lines of the summary one by one, find the sentence in the text where the same content appears, and put them side by side.
x-e-e5-02.s.s1.hint.1: Mark the words that show time (morning, afternoon, all day) and compare them with the text.
x-e-e5-02.s.s1.explain: Line 2 is wrong. In the text it rained only in the morning and stopped in the afternoon, so Ben fished in the afternoon. Lines 1, 3, and 4 match the text.
x-e-e5-02.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite the wrong line in English so that it fits the text. One or two sentences is enough.
x-e-e5-02.s.s2.hint.0: First find when it rained and when it stopped in the text.
x-e-e5-02.s.s2.hint.1: Put those two times (morning, afternoon) into your corrected sentence.
x-e-e5-02.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Does it include the fact that it rained only in the morning?
x-e-e5-02.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Does it fit the flow that, as a result, he fished in the afternoon?
x-e-e5-02.s.s2.modelNote.1: Another answer that fixed it with 'only in the morning'.

x-e-e5-03.title: A bike shop ad: check Mia's plan
x-e-e5-03.topic: Reading short texts, ads, and messages
x-e-e5-03.goal: Compare the conditions in an ad (today only, closing time) with a friend's plan line by line, find the parts that do not fit, and tell her in English.
x-e-e5-03.material:
Mia saw this ad on the street (written as text only, with no picture).

RIDE BIKE SHOP
BIG SALE! All bikes 30% off.
Today only!
Open 9 a.m. - 6 p.m.
12 Park Street

(30% is read 'thirty percent'.)
x-e-e5-03.thinking.0: Compare the wording of the ad with each line of the plan
x-e-e5-03.thinking.1: Check conditions such as today only and 6 p.m.
x-e-e5-03.thinking.2: Tell what does not fit, with evidence
x-e-e5-03.prereq.0: The meanings of sale, open, bike, and off
x-e-e5-03.s.s1.prompt: Mia told her plan in four lines. Choose one line that does not match the ad. (There may be two or more lines that do not match. You may choose just one.)
x-e-e5-03.s.s1.hint.1: Among Mia's lines, compare the lines that talk about a date or a time with that wording in the ad.
x-e-e5-03.s.s1.explain: Line 3 is wrong because of 'Today only!' (tomorrow is not on sale), and line 4 is wrong because the shop closes at 6 p.m. but she says she will go at 7 p.m. Lines 1 and 2 match the ad.
x-e-e5-03.s.s2.prompt: Reply to Mia in English. Tell her one thing in her plan that will not work, with the reason.
x-e-e5-03.s.s2.hint.0: Pick one phrase from the ad that is the problem and bring it in as it is.
x-e-e5-03.s.s2.hint.1: Use so, which means 'so I can't ...', to connect it in one sentence.
x-e-e5-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you say which phrase of the ad is the reason it will not work?
x-e-e5-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you add a way to fix it (going today, going before 6)? (optional)
x-e-e5-03.s.s2.modelNote.1: An answer that even gave a way to fix it.
x-e-e5-03.s.s1.hint.0: As you read each line of the ad, underline the phrases that mention a date or a time.

x-e-e5-04.title: Your thinking changes as you read the poster
x-e-e5-04.goal: Change your judgment each time the poster's information is revealed step by step, and make an English question that checks information that is not on the poster.
x-e-e5-04.material: Jun is not a member of Green Library. His friend Ara is a member of Green Library. The two of them are going to read the poster in front of the library one line at a time.
x-e-e5-04.thinking.0: Change your judgment each time you meet new information
x-e-e5-04.thinking.2: Tell what is already answered from what you still do not know
x-e-e5-04.prereq.0: The meanings of free, member, friend, and won (KRW)
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.prompt: The information is revealed one piece at a time. Each time, predict the money Jun will pay using the information so far.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.hint.0: Check whether the sentence that is new this time changes your earlier judgment.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.hint.1: Read carefully to tell whether it is Jun or Ara who is a member.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.0.info: Poster title: FREE ART CAMP! This Sunday. Green Library.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.0.ask: Looking only at this title, will Jun pay money?
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.0.after: From the title alone it looks 'free', but there may be a condition in the small print.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.0.o.a: I think he does not need to pay.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: This is a first guess that judges only by the FREE in the title.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.0.o.b: I need to read more to know.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: This is a judgment that saw there could be a condition outside the title.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: There are no words yet that tell him to pay.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.1.info: Small print: Free for Green Library members. Other children: 5,000 won.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.1.ask: Jun is not a member. Now, how much will Jun pay?
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.1.after: It is free only for members and 5,000 won for other children, so Jun pays 5,000 won.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You may have missed the condition that it is free only for members.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: I found the line for children who are not members and connected it.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: There are no words saying he is not allowed to join.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.2.info: Bottom line: Members can bring one friend for free.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: If Jun goes with Ara, who is a member, how much will he pay?
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.2.after: A member can bring one friend for free. Ara is a member, so if Jun goes with Ara it is free.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.reflect: You changed your 'free' judgment on the second line, and changed it again on the third line. Look back at which words changed your judgment, and what was missing when you first trusted only the title.
x-e-e5-04.s.s2.prompt: There is information the poster does not give yet (for example, what time it starts, how to sign up). Write one English sentence that is a question checking this kind of information. Leave out questions about money, because those are already answered.
x-e-e5-04.s.s2.hint.0: Look for whether the poster has the 'date' but whether it has the 'time' or 'how to sign up'.
x-e-e5-04.s.s2.hint.1: Pick one thing you still do not know, write it as a question, and put a question mark.
x-e-e5-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Is the answer to my question really not on the poster?
x-e-e5-04.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Does the question clearly ask about only one thing?
x-e-e5-04.s.s2.modelNote.1: A question that asks how to sign up.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Check again whether the new line applies to Jun's case.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.2.o.b: 5,000 won (because Jun is not a member)
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You may have looked only at the condition in the earlier line and not taken the new line into account.
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.2.o.c: 0 won (because he is a friend that Ara brings)
x-e-e5-04.s.s1.st.2.r.c: It connects the new line with the relationship between the two people.

x-e-e5-05.title: Main idea and supporting sentences in a school garden text
x-e-e5-05.goal: Choose the main idea from the sentences, separate the details that support the main idea from plain facts, and then make a supporting sentence yourself.
x-e-e5-05.thinking.0: Tell the main idea from the details
x-e-e5-05.thinking.1: Sort out supporting information from unrelated information
x-e-e5-05.thinking.2: Make a detail sentence that fits the main idea
x-e-e5-05.prereq.0: The meanings of garden, plant, insect, and seed
x-e-e5-05.prereq.1: The experience that a paragraph is made of one big idea and smaller ideas
x-e-e5-05.s.s1.prompt: Which sentence best fits the main idea of the whole text?
x-e-e5-05.s.s1.hint.0: Compare whether each choice talks about only one part of the text or covers the whole text.
x-e-e5-05.s.s1.hint.1: Connect one choice with every other sentence of the text, and find the one that connects with the most sentences.
x-e-e5-05.s.s1.r.a: This one looks at the main point as a detail in one sentence of the text.
x-e-e5-05.s.s1.r.b: This is a fact that tells a place. Check whether it connects to the other sentences.
x-e-e5-05.s.s1.r.c: This one looks at the main point as just one thing in the daily routine.
x-e-e5-05.s.s1.r.d: This choice thought about whether the content of several sentences can be tied into one.
x-e-e5-05.s.s1.explain: Planting in the garden, watering, observing and writing about insects, and learning what bees do are all tied together by the big idea 'the garden is a place for learning'. The other choices are each only one fact among them.
x-e-e5-05.s.s2.prompt: Choose all the sentences that support the main idea 'The garden helps students learn.'
x-e-e5-05.s.s2.hint.0: Read each choice and ask yourself, 'Is this evidence that students learn?'
x-e-e5-05.s.s2.hint.1: First cross out the choices that are true but have nothing to do with learning.
x-e-e5-05.s.s2.r.a: Think about whether it is a fact that connects to learning.
x-e-e5-05.s.s2.r.b: This choice thought about whether what students do is evidence of learning.
x-e-e5-05.s.s2.r.c: I found and connected the sentence that directly says what was learned.
x-e-e5-05.s.s2.r.d: Think about whether the information about the place shows learning.
x-e-e5-05.s.s2.explain: Observing and writing about insects and what they learned about bees are evidence of learning. That the garden is small and next to the gym are facts, but they are information that has nothing to do with learning.
x-e-e5-05.s.s3.prompt: Make one new English sentence that supports the main idea 'The garden helps students learn.' It is fine if it is not in the text.
x-e-e5-05.s.s3.hint.0: Think of one thing students can see or one thing they can do in the garden.
x-e-e5-05.s.s3.hint.1: Write it in one sentence using a verb like 'learn, observe, write'.
x-e-e5-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Is my sentence evidence that students learn in the garden?
x-e-e5-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did you avoid just saying the size or location of the garden?
x-e-e5-05.s.s3.modelNote.1: Another good sentence that wrote about an observing activity.

x-e-e5-06.title: Two Swim Day notices: what is different?
x-e-e5-06.goal: Compare two notices item by item, tell the 'real differences' from things that 'look different but are not contradictions', and write a checking question in English.
x-e-e5-06.material:
Two Swim Day notices came from Mina's school.

Notice A (school office)
Swim Day. Date: Friday, June 7.
Meet: school gate, 8:30 a.m.
Bring: swimsuit, towel, swimming cap.

Notice B (homeroom teacher)
Swim Day is on Friday, June 7. The bus leaves at 9:00 a.m. Please bring a swimsuit and a towel. If it rains, we will go on June 14.
x-e-e5-06.thinking.0: Compare the two texts item by item
x-e-e5-06.thinking.1: Tell apart the same content, different content, and content in only one of them
x-e-e5-06.thinking.2: Recognize differences that are not contradictions
x-e-e5-06.prereq.0: The meanings of swimsuit, towel, cap, and gate
x-e-e5-06.prereq.1: Reading dates (June 7 = the seventh of June)
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.prompt: When you compare the two notices, choose all the 'real differences' (information in only one, or information that does not match).
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.hint.0: Draw a table with four items, date, time, things to bring, and what happens if it rains, and fill in A and B.
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.o.a: Date: A says June 7 and B says June 14.
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.r.a: Read again in what case the date June 14 in B is used.
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.o.b: Swimming cap: it is written only in A.
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.r.b: I matched and compared the things-to-bring lines of the two texts item by item.
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.o.c: Time: A says 8:30 and B says 9:00, so they contradict each other.
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.r.c: Check whether 8:30 and 9:00 are talking about the same thing (meeting/leaving).
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.o.d: If it rains: it is only in B.
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.r.d: I found the information that is in only one of them.
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.explain: The swimming cap is written only in A, and the plan for rain is only in B. The June 14 in B is only the date for when it rains and is not different from A, and 8:30 is the time to meet at the school gate while 9:00 is the time the bus leaves, so they do not contradict each other.
x-e-e5-06.s.s2.prompt: Write a short question text to the teacher in English. Check one thing that the two notices say differently or that is in only one of them.
x-e-e5-06.s.s2.hint.0: Pick one of the 'real differences' you chose in s1.
x-e-e5-06.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Does my question deal with a part where the two notices say different things?
x-e-e5-06.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Can the teacher answer with 'yes/no' or in one sentence?
x-e-e5-06.s.s2.modelNote.1: Another good question that checks the plan for when it rains.
x-e-e5-06.s.s1.hint.1: For each item, check whether the "thing" that A and B talk about is the same, or whether they talk about different things.
x-e-e5-06.s.s2.hint.1: Write one question as an English question sentence and put a question mark at the end.
x-e-e5-06.s.s2.modelNote.2: A question that checks both the meeting place that only A has and the bus that only B has.

x-e-e5-07.title: The meeting notice changed: tell Sam
x-e-e5-07.goal: Judge from evidence which of two notices with different dates to follow, and tell a friend who has only seen the old poster what changed, in English.
x-e-e5-07.material:
Sam is a new member of the book club. Sam has only seen the old poster on the hallway wall. You are a club member, so you saw the new note too.

Poster (Sep. 1)
Book Club. Tuesday, 4:00 p.m. Room 5. New members welcome!

Note (Sep. 20)
CHANGE! From next week, Book Club is on Wednesday at 4:00 p.m. in the library.
x-e-e5-07.thinking.0: Judge which notice is newest from the dates and the change mark
x-e-e5-07.thinking.1: Tell old information from new information
x-e-e5-07.thinking.2: Write simply, with only the information the receiver needs
x-e-e5-07.prereq.0: The meanings of change, library, Room, and Wednesday/Tuesday
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.prompt: Which notice should Sam follow next week?
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.hint.0: Compare the dates written on the two notices and see which one was made later.
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.o.a: Follow both notices. Go to the meeting on both Tuesday and Wednesday.
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.r.a: Think about whether you can combine the two notices into one schedule.
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.o.d: Trust neither, and do not go until the teacher tells you.
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.r.d: This is a choice that puts off checking even though there is evidence.
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.explain: The note is later, Sep. 20, and says 'CHANGE!'. So the club is now on Wednesday at 4, in the library. That it has been on the wall for a long time is not evidence that the information is up to date.
x-e-e5-07.s.s2.prompt: Write Sam a short message in English. Tell him the new day and place, and also say that it is different from the poster. Use easy words.
x-e-e5-07.s.s2.hint.0: Write the old information Sam already knows and the new information, one sentence each.
x-e-e5-07.s.s2.hint.1: Take the day and place words straight from the note.
x-e-e5-07.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Can Sam tell where and when to go just by reading this message?
x-e-e5-07.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you write it so it cannot be confused with the old information (Tuesday, Room 5)?
x-e-e5-07.s.s2.modelNote.1: Another answer that was written short and easy.
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.hint.1: Compare what each of the two notices says about the earlier schedule.
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.o.b: Follow the September 20 note. It came out later and says it is a change.
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.r.b: You picked out the latest information based on the date and the change mark.
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.o.c: Follow the September 1 poster. It is posted on the wall and is the originally set schedule, so it is the most reliable.
x-e-e5-07.s.s1.r.c: Look back at what you used as your basis: where it is posted, or when it was made.

x-e-e5-08.title: 'Meet at the cinema!' What should I ask?
x-e-e5-08.goal: Sort out what information is missing from a friend's message, and write the questions you really need in English.
x-e-e5-08.material:
Dana and Eli are classmates. In the town where Dana lives, there are two cinemas: Star Cinema and Moon Cinema.

Eli sent Dana a text.

Eli: "Let's see a movie on Saturday! I will buy the tickets. Meet me at the cinema!"
x-e-e5-08.thinking.0: Tell what the message already says from what is missing
x-e-e5-08.thinking.1: Choose the information you really need for the purpose (meeting)
x-e-e5-08.thinking.2: Write two needed questions in English
x-e-e5-08.prereq.0: The meanings of cinema, ticket, and meet
x-e-e5-08.prereq.1: Question forms such as What time ...? / Which ...?
x-e-e5-08.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the things Dana must ask in order to be sure to meet Eli on Saturday.
x-e-e5-08.s.s1.hint.0: First mark the information the text already gives (the day, the tickets).
x-e-e5-08.s.s1.hint.1: Keep only what you need for 'meeting'. Leave out questions that would be nice to have but that you could meet without.
x-e-e5-08.s.s1.r.a: This choice noticed that the information needed for meeting is the time.
x-e-e5-08.s.s1.r.b: This choice connected the fact that there are two cinemas with the text.
x-e-e5-08.s.s1.r.c: Check again whether the text says who buys the tickets.
x-e-e5-08.s.s1.r.d: It is a nice question to have, but think about whether it is really needed for meeting.
x-e-e5-08.s.s1.explain: The text has the day (Saturday) and that Eli buys the tickets, but it does not have what time they meet and which cinema. There are two cinemas in the town, so you must ask both. Your favorite movie is not really needed for meeting.
x-e-e5-08.s.s2.prompt: Write in English the reply Dana sends to Eli. Include both of the questions you really need.
x-e-e5-08.s.s2.hint.0: Write each of the two you chose in s1 as a one-sentence question.
x-e-e5-08.s.s2.hint.1: A question about time can start with What time, and a question about place can start with Which or Where.
x-e-e5-08.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Are both the time and cinema questions in it?
x-e-e5-08.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Can Eli answer right away after reading just this reply?
x-e-e5-08.s.s2.modelNote.1: Another good answer that asked about the place and the start time.

x-e-e5-09.title: Asking the teacher to change your seat
x-e-e5-09.topic: Making a request with a reason
x-e-e5-09.goal: Choose request words and a specific reason that fit the other person (the teacher) and the situation, and rewrite a harsh phrase into a polite request.
x-e-e5-09.material: Hana sits in a seat at the back of the classroom and cannot see the writing on the board well. The sentence Hana first wrote is this: "Move my seat." She wants to ask her teacher (Mr. Kim) to change her seat.
x-e-e5-09.thinking.0: Evaluate whether both the request and the reason are there
x-e-e5-09.thinking.1: Fix the tone to fit the receiver
x-e-e5-09.thinking.2: Write a specific reason the other person can judge
x-e-e5-09.prereq.0: The meaning of Could I ...? / May I ...?
x-e-e5-09.prereq.2: The meanings of board, seat, and sit
x-e-e5-09.s.s1.prompt: Which one is the most suitable request to a teacher?
x-e-e5-09.s.s1.hint.0: For each choice, mark whether it has both the 'request words' and the 'reason'.
x-e-e5-09.s.s1.hint.1: Think about the fact that the listener is a teacher, and compare the tone too.
